label: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
output:
**Re: Tolu_Aspirant — "Is anybody in Biology 100L that wanted Medicine?"**

Good evening Tolu. I'll answer properly, because you asked for honesty and because nobody was honest with me when I was exactly where you are sitting right now.

**First, my own story so you know I'm not just talking from a textbook.**

I wrote JAMB in 2025. I scored 251. I applied for Medicine and Surgery. I had told everybody — my mother, my father's brother, the whole church — that I was going to study Medicine. Then I checked the portal and I was given **Biology**. Federal university in Lagos.

Tolu, that night I locked myself in my cousin's room in Surulere and cried until I had no tears left. I did not eat. I did not go to church that Sunday. For about two months my mother was still telling people in church that I am doing Medicine, and I had to beg her to stop, because every time somebody asked her "how is Amaka?" she would say "she's in Medicine" and I would have to sit there and correct her. That part nobody warns you about. It's not the courses that break you, it's the announcing.

**Now let me answer the transfer question properly, because that's the one that will decide your life.**

Kingsley says transfer is a myth. That is not true, and I don't want you to make your decision on a forum post — including mine. But favour says "just read hard" and leave it there. That is too simple, and if you go in with that mindset you will be blindsided in second semester when the space doesn't come.

This is what our level adviser told us, and these are the actual three things:

1. **CGPA of at least 4.5 out of 5** in 100L.
2. **Space must be available.** This is the part people never mention. You can have 5.0 and still not move if there is no vacancy in the department that year.
3. **You must meet the cut-offs for Medicine in both JAMB and post-UTME.** Not just one. Both.

And the numbers she gave us: last year, about **six people moved in from the whole faculty**. Over **forty applied**. So roughly one in six. That is not zero — that's a real door — but it is also not a guaranteed path you can plan your whole life around.

Tolu, one thing about your own score: you said 268. I scored 251, so you are already ahead of me there. But **268 by itself doesn't establish your eligibility**. Please go and check your university's Medicine cut-off for JAMB *and* your department's post-UTME cut-off. Some schools ask for 280+ in JAMB for Medicine, some ask 270, some ask lower but then use post-UTME as the real filter. If you clear both, your file is competitive. If you don't, no amount of 5.0 will help you because it's a screening criterion before they even look at your grades. Check that this week. It's free and it's the single most important fact you don't have yet.

My own CGPA after first semester is **4.31**. Not 4.5. I'm still grinding. So even if the space comes, I still have work to do.

**What Biology 100L is actually like** (in case you're deciding on the basis of pure dread):

Courses: BIO 101, CHM 101, PHY 101, MTH 101, GST. Biology itself I can speak for — the lectures are fine. **Physics and Maths are the ones that will deal with people.** I went from arts, I nearly cried over MTH 101 in my first week. Nobody warned me that a "science" course would have this much calculation in it.

Money so you can budget: lab coat was **6,500**, dissecting kit **9,000**, plus money for the practical manual and materials. Not fatal, but it's real, and it comes before you get any benefit from the course.

**The turning point for me, and I don't know if it will be for you.**

First BIO practical we dissected toads. One guy in my group fainted and they had to take him outside. I was fine. And somewhere in that session I realised, oh — I actually like this thing. I like knowing how the body works, cell by cell. Right now I am enjoying **genetics and cell biology** more than I expected I would, and honestly there are days I feel like I understand something that matters.

So I won't lie to you: Biology is not a punishment. It is not the consolation prize they are pretending it is. It's a good course. If you came in expecting Medicine, it may even be more interesting for you, because Medicine is mostly applied Biology anyway.

**But I will also not lie to you the other way.** Transfer is real. Transfer is also hard. **Nobody should accept Biology thinking transfer is automatic.** Accept it thinking you are starting a race with three hurdles in front of you, and you can clear them, but you cannot skip them.

**On rewriting.**

My secondary school classmate Ifeoma had a Pharmacy offer. She rejected it to rewrite for Medicine. She has written JAMB two more times. She is still at home. I love her, but that decision cost her two years and it is still costing her.

That is not me saying rewriting is wrong. **Rewriting is not wrong if you are ready** — if you are ready for another full year of preparing, if your mind is settled, if you can carry it. But favour is right about one thing: staying home is not as easy as people say. You will watch your mates go to school. You will see their pictures. Your parents will start asking questions. It wears on you.

So don't rewrite because you are crying today. Don't accept because your dad said so on Wednesday. Sit down with both options and decide with facts.

**The question I want you to sit with (please don't take this the wrong way):**

Do you actually want to *be* a doctor, or do you want your parents to be able to say "my daughter is a doctor"? Those are two different things and only you know which one is driving you. Because if it's mostly the second one, you might get very far in Biology and still be unhappy, and then the transfer will feel like a trap instead of a plan. If it's the first one, then Medicine is worth fighting for and this is worth being honest and hard about.

**What I would do in the next two weeks, in this order:**

1. Go to your faculty/department and ask for the **exact transfer rules for your own school** — the CGPA, the space quota, the JAMB and post-UTME cut-offs, and how the application is ranked when more people qualify than there are slots. Ask for it in writing if you can. **Don't trust forum people for this, including me.** Our schools differ. My university cannot speak for yours.
2. Check the Medicine cut-offs (JAMB and post-UTME) for your school.
3. Then talk to your dad — not the argument you had on Wednesday, but with the actual facts in your hand. He is trying to protect you, he just doesn't have the information you have now.
4. Do not reject anything today on the strength of a forum thread. You have two weeks. Use them to get facts.

**Finally, Tolu — whatever you choose, it is not the end of the world.** I promise you that. There are people older than us with Biology degrees doing well, and there are people in Medicine who are not happy. The exam result that came out on your portal is one result, not a verdict on your life. Take a breath. Eat something. Sleep. Then go and get the facts.

I'm in Biology 100L, I wanted Medicine, I'm still here and I'm okay. If you want to ask me anything else — about the courses, the money, the practicals, the adviser — just tag me. I don't mind at all.

**Amaka_Bio100**

reasons: The piece says 'I went from arts', which conflicts with the writer having applied for Medicine and Surgery in JAMB, a science-subject application. It also invents a 'Wednesday' argument with Tolu's dad that the thread never mentions.
